name: 皮埃尔-奥古斯特·雷诺阿

points.title: 童年时光
points.description: 皮埃尔-奥古斯特·雷诺阿1841年2月25日出生于法国利摩日的一个工人家庭。他的父亲是裁缝，母亲是裁缝学徒。雷诺阿是家庭六个孩子中的第二个，童年生活相对贫困。四岁时，全家迁往巴黎，在卢浮宫附近居住。这段早期生活虽然贫困，但雷诺阿后来回忆说，这段经历培养了他对生活的热爱和对美的敏感，这些特质后来成为他艺术创作的核心。
points.descriptionEn: Pierre-Auguste Renoir was born on February 25, 1841, in Limoges, France, into a working-class family. His father was a tailor and his mother was a seamstress's apprentice. Renoir was the second of six children in the family. When he was four years old, the family moved to Paris, settling near the Louvre. Although his early life was impoverished, Renoir later recalled that these experiences cultivated his love for life and sensitivity to beauty, which became central to his artistic creations.

points.title: 艺术学徒期
points.description: 1862年，雷诺阿进入巴黎查尔斯·格莱尔(Charles Gleyre)的画室学习，在那里结识了克劳德·莫奈、阿尔弗雷德·西斯莱和弗雷德里克·巴齐耶。这四位年轻艺术家后来成为印象派的核心成员。在格莱尔的指导下，雷诺阿掌握了基本的绘画技巧，但他很快开始发展自己独特的风格，注重光线和色彩的运用。这一时期，他创作了《青蛙塘》(La Grenouillère)等早期作品，开始展现他对户外场景和人物互动的敏锐观察。
points.descriptionEn: In 1862, Renoir entered the studio of Charles Gleyre in Paris, where he met Claude Monet, Alfred Sisley, and Frédéric Bazille. These four young artists would later become core members of the Impressionist movement. Under Gleyre's guidance, Renoir mastered basic painting techniques, but he soon began developing his unique style, focusing on the use of light and color. During this period, he created early works such as 'La Grenouillère' (The Frog Pond), beginning to showcase his keen observation of outdoor scenes and human interactions.

points.title: 印象派探索
points.description: 1870年代初期，雷诺阿与莫奈等艺术家一起在枫丹白露森林附近创作，这是印象派风格形成的关键时期。他们专注于捕捉光线在物体表面的变化，以及在特定时间和天气条件下的视觉效果。雷诺阿在这一时期创作了《煎饼磨坊的舞会》(Bal du moulin de la Galette)，这幅作品成为印象派的代表作之一。1874年，雷诺阿参加了第一届印象派画展，展出了多幅作品，虽然当时评论界反应冷淡，但这些作品奠定了他在艺术史上的重要地位。
points.descriptionEn: In the early 1870s, Renoir worked near the Fontainebleau Forest with artists like Monet, a crucial period for the formation of Impressionist style. They focused on capturing the changes of light on surfaces and visual effects under specific times and weather conditions. During this period, Renoir created 'Bal du moulin de la Galette' (Dance at Le Moulin de la Galette), which became one of the representative works of Impressionism. In 1874, Renoir participated in the first Impressionist exhibition, displaying multiple works. Although the critical reception was冷淡 at the time, these works established his important place in art history.

points.place: 阿尔及尔、意大利、西班牙
points.title: 艺术之旅
points.description: 1881年至1883年，雷诺阿进行了重要的艺术之旅，先后访问了阿尔及尔、意大利和西班牙。在阿尔及尔，他被北非的光线和色彩所吸引，创作了《阿尔及尔女人》(Femmes d'Alger)。在意大利，他深入研究拉斐尔等文艺复兴大师的作品，特别是对线条和构图的重视影响了他的创作。在西班牙，他受到委拉斯开兹作品的启发，开始更加注重人物的描绘和细节表现。这次旅行对雷诺阿的艺术风格产生了深远影响，使他开始融合印象派的色彩技巧与古典主义的线条美。
points.descriptionEn: From 1881 to 1883, Renoir undertook an important artistic journey, visiting Algiers, Italy, and Spain. In Algiers, he was captivated by the light and colors of North Africa, creating 'Femmes d'Alger' (Women of Algiers). In Italy, he studied the works of Renaissance masters like Raphael, particularly their emphasis on lines and composition, which influenced his own work. In Spain, he was inspired by Velázquez's paintings, beginning to focus more on figure depiction and detail. This journey profoundly impacted Renoir's artistic style, leading him to blend Impressionist color techniques with classical linear beauty.

points.title: 风格转变
points.description: 1890年代，雷诺阿的艺术风格发生了明显转变，他开始更加注重线条和形式，这一时期被称为他的'干时期'(Ingres period)。他受到安格尔等古典主义画家的影响，创作了《大浴女》(Les Grandes Baigneuses)等作品，这些作品展现出更加严谨的构图和更加细腻的人物描绘。同时，雷诺阿也开始探索雕塑艺术，创作了一些小型雕塑作品。这一时期，他的健康状况开始恶化，患上了严重的风湿病，但他的创作热情不减，反而更加专注于创作，完成了许多重要作品。
points.descriptionEn: During the 1890s, Renoir's artistic style underwent a significant transformation, as he began to focus more on lines and form, a period known as his 'Ingres period.' Influenced by classical painters like Ingres, he created works such as 'Les Grandes Baigneuses' (The Large Bathers), which show more rigorous composition and more delicate figure depiction. At the same time, Renoir also began exploring sculpture, creating some small sculptural works. During this period, his health began to deteriorate as he suffered from severe rheumatoid arthritis, but his creative enthusiasm did not diminish; instead, he became more focused on his work, completing many important pieces.

points.title: 晚年创作
points.description: 1910年后，雷诺阿的健康状况进一步恶化，风湿病使他几乎无法握笔。然而，在助手安德烈·马索(André Massot)的帮助下，他继续创作。1919年，雷诺阿在巴黎卢森堡博物馆看到自己的作品被展出，这是他生前唯一一次看到自己的作品在博物馆展出。同年12月3日，雷诺阿在法国南部的加尼(Cagnes-sur-Mer)去世，享年78岁。晚年的雷诺阿虽然身体受限，但创作风格更加成熟，作品如《浴女》(Bathers)系列展现出对生命和美的永恒追求，成为他艺术生涯的完美收官。
points.descriptionEn: After 1910, Renoir's health further deteriorated, and rheumatoid arthritis made it nearly impossible for him to hold a brush. However, with the assistance of his assistant André Massot, he continued to create. In 1919, Renoir saw his own work exhibited at the Musée du Luxembourg in Paris, the only time he witnessed his own works in a museum during his lifetime. On December 3 of the same year, Renoir died in Cagnes-sur-Mer, southern France, at the age of 78. Although physically limited in his later years, Renoir's artistic style became more mature. Works such as his 'Bathers' series showed an eternal pursuit of life and beauty, serving as a perfect conclusion to his artistic career.

appraisal.zh: 雷诺阿是印象派最具人情味的代表画家之一，他将印象派的光影与古典线条相融，笔下女性和儿童洋溢着温暖的人性光辉，晚年病痛中仍坚持创作。不过也有研究者指出，他的作品有时过于甜美理想化，女性形象被视为程式化并带有男性凝视的痕迹，后期转向古典风格亦被看作疏离前卫。总体而言，他仍被公认为西方艺术史上最重要的画家之一，其作品成为印象派与19世纪末法国中产阶级生活的经典象征。
appraisal.en: Renoir is celebrated as one of the most humanistic Impressionists, fusing Impressionist light with classical line; his women and children radiate warmth, and he painted on despite illness. Yet some researchers note his work can be overly sweet and idealized, his female figures formulaic and shaped by the male gaze, and his later classical turn a departure from the avant-garde. Still, he is widely recognized as one of the most important painters in Western art, his work a classic emblem of Impressionism and late 19th-century French bourgeois life.

supporter.zh: 雷诺阿被誉为印象派大师中最具人情味的画家之一。他的作品充满了对生活的热爱和对美的赞颂，尤其是对女性和儿童的描绘，展现出温暖的人性光辉。雷诺阿的艺术贡献在于他将印象派的光影技巧与古典主义的线条美完美融合，创造出独特的艺术语言。他的作品不仅影响了后世无数画家，也为现代艺术的发展开辟了新道路。雷诺阿的精神遗产在于他即使在病痛中仍坚持创作，展现了艺术家对美的永恒追求和坚韧不拔的精神。
supporter.en: Renoir is celebrated as one of the most humanistic painters among the Impressionist masters. His works are filled with a love for life and an admiration for beauty, particularly his depictions of women and children, which reveal a warm human radiance. Renoir's artistic contribution lies in his perfect fusion of Impressionist light and shadow techniques with classical linear beauty, creating a unique artistic language. His works not only influenced countless later artists but also paved new paths for the development of modern art. Renoir's legacy is his persistent pursuit of beauty despite physical suffering, demonstrating the indomitable spirit of an artist.

critic.zh: 批评者认为雷诺阿的作品有时过于甜美和理想化，缺乏对社会现实的深刻反思。他的女性形象常被批评为过于程式化和男性凝视的产物，反映了当时社会对女性的刻板印象。此外，雷诺阿在艺术生涯后期转向古典主义风格，被一些评论家视为对前卫艺术的背叛。他的作品也被批评为过于注重形式美而缺乏思想深度，与同时代更具社会意识的艺术家相比显得肤浅。这些批评反映了雷诺阿艺术中的局限性，以及他与更激进艺术运动的距离。
critic.en: Critics argue that Renoir's works can be overly sweet and idealized, lacking deep reflection on social reality. His female figures are often criticized as formulaic and products of the male gaze, reflecting the stereotypes of women in contemporary society. Furthermore, Renoir's shift toward classical style in his later career has been seen by some critics as a betrayal of avant-garde art. His works are also criticized for focusing too much on formal beauty without intellectual depth, appearing superficial compared to more socially conscious artists of his time. These criticisms reflect the limitations in Renoir's art and his distance from more radical art movements.

objective.zh: 在历史学界和流行文化中，雷诺阿被定义为印象派的标志性人物之一，其作品代表了19世纪末法国中产阶级生活的美好图景。他的艺术风格经历了从印象派到更注重线条和形式的转变，展现了艺术家在不同时期的探索与成长。雷诺阿的作品已成为全球艺术博物馆的珍藏品，他的名字与印象派紧密相连，成为艺术教育的经典案例。在流行文化中，雷诺阿的形象被广泛传播，他的作品被用于各种商业和文化产品中，成为西方艺术传统的象征之一。雷诺阿的艺术成就和历史地位得到了广泛认可，他被公认为西方艺术史上最重要的画家之一。
objective.en: In academic and popular culture, Renoir is defined as one of the iconic figures of Impressionism, whose works represent the beautiful vision of French bourgeois life in the late 19th century. His artistic style evolved from Impressionism to a greater emphasis on lines and form, reflecting the artist's exploration and growth at different periods. Renoir's works have become treasures in global art museums, and his name is closely associated with Impressionism, serving as a classic case in art education. In popular culture, Renoir's image is widely disseminated, and his works appear in various commercial and cultural products, becoming a symbol of Western artistic tradition. Renoir's artistic achievements and historical position are widely recognized, and he is regarded as one of the most important painters in Western art history.

self.zh: 我画画是为了取悦自己，但我也希望我的画能给人们带来快乐。
self.en: I paint for myself, but I want everyone to be able to see my paintings and be happy.
